chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn al-Muthanna al-Attar narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
People will miss an Imam who attends the seasons (of pilgrimage), he sees them but they do not see him.

key_terms.الْمَوَاسِمَ: the seasons (specifically referring to Hajj and major gatherings)
key_terms.وَلَا يَرَوْنَهُ: and they do not see him
key_terms.يَفْتَقِدُ: to miss or long for the absence of

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the people's longing for the Imam during the occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual paradox of the Major Occultation, where the Imam is physically present among the people during key rituals like Hajj but remains hidden from their direct sight due to divine decree. This concept of 'ghaybah' (concealment) serves as a test of faith, emphasizing that the Imam's guidance continues despite the lack of visible, constant access, a theme central to Shia eschatology regarding the return of the Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (13) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from al-Hasan bin Muhammad as-Sayrafi from Yahya bin al-Muthanna al-Attar from Abdullah bin Bukayr from Obayd bin Zurara that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “People will miss an imam. He attends the seasons (of hajj). He sees the people but they do not see him.”
